data.title: Keystroke Capture Possible Without Detection
data.summary:
Keystrokes could be captured from a standard user session without elevation and without
detection, yielding credentials that no password policy or rotation addresses.
data.description:
Keylogging defeats credential controls rather than circumventing them. Complexity, length
and rotation are all irrelevant to a credential captured as it is typed, and the same
applies to one-time codes entered manually.

It requires no elevation, since capturing input within the user's own session is ordinary
application behaviour, and it produces no network signature until collected data is sent.

The durable mitigation is to remove the typed secret: phishing-resistant authenticators
that use a cryptographic exchange rather than a typed value are not captured by this
technique at all.
data.recommendation:
* Deploy phishing-resistant authentication so that the secret is never typed and therefore
  cannot be captured.
* Enable behavioural detection for input capture hooks in the endpoint product.
* Restrict the ability of standard users to run arbitrary executables, which is the
  precondition.
data.short_recommendation: Deploy phishing-resistant authentication so secrets are never typed.
